transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep losing my temper over little things. Like at work, I yelled at one of my employees for putting stock on the wrong shelf, and afterward I was shaking. That’s really not how I usually treat people, and it scared me.
Have you been acting impulsively in other areas of your life, beyond just getting angry?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself doing anything impulsive, like spending or taking risks or anything like that. It’s mainly been the anger that feels out of control.
Do you think your coworkers or friends would describe you as a hot-headed or aggressive person in general?

No, I really don’t think they would. I’m not usually hot-headed or aggressive. That’s why this has been so upsetting — lately I keep blowing up over little things, like that stock-shelf thing at work, and afterward I was shaking because it felt so unlike me.
Have you always had trouble managing your emotions, or is this something that has developed recently?

This is recent. I haven’t always been like this. I’m usually pretty steady with people, but lately I keep blowing up over things that shouldn’t be a big deal. Like when I yelled at my employee over the stock being on the wrong shelf… afterward I was shaking, because that’s just not how I normally act.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed. I’ve been really upset and not feeling like myself, but I’m not sure it’s sadness exactly.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to act on?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had upsetting thoughts, but not like urges I feel I have to act on. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and won't go away?

Yes. The fire keeps coming into my head when I’m not even thinking about it. Like I’ll pick up a pan, or even just be looking at a spreadsheet, and suddenly I’m right back there—smelling smoke and seeing the kitchen filling up. It’s like I can’t stop it once it starts.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when you have these angry outbursts or the recurring thoughts of the fire?

Yeah… sometimes. It’s not always during anger, but when those thoughts come up, or even when I’m just walking through the store, it can feel like I’m watching myself from a few feet away. Like the aisles and the customers are there, but they don’t feel totally real, and I’m just moving through everything on automatic.
Can you tell me more about the fire that keeps coming into your head?

It just comes into my head suddenly. Like I’ll be doing something normal—picking up a pan, or opening a spreadsheet at work—and then it’s like I’m back there. I can smell the smoke and see the kitchen filling up, and it happens before I can stop it. It’s really hard to shake once it starts.
Have you been avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of the fire?

Yes. I’ve been avoiding the house, mostly. I also can’t bring myself to open the mortgage folder, and even the herbs out on my patio bother me now because they remind me of that day. Anything connected to it makes my chest tighten, and I just… I can’t make myself go near it.
Have your symptoms been causing problems for you at work or in your relationships?

Yes. It’s definitely causing problems. I missed a vendor meeting at work, and I actually walked out before finishing a shift because I just couldn’t keep going. And at home… I can’t face going back to the damaged house, so all the responsibilities there are just piling up. It feels like it’s getting ahead of me faster than I can handle.
How long have you been experiencing these angry outbursts and recurring thoughts of the fire?

It’s been about two weeks now. It started right after the kitchen fire, during that first weekend we were working on the house. Since then the thoughts keep coming back, and the anger’s been happening too.
Do you experience any physical symptoms, like a racing heart or headaches, when you have these angry outbursts?

Yes. When I blow up, I can feel it in my body. Like, I yelled at one of my employees for putting stock on the wrong shelf, which is not like me at all, and afterward I was shaking. It felt way out of proportion.
Are there any specific activities or situations that you're avoiding because they remind you of the fire?

Yes. I’ve been avoiding the house as much as I can. I also can’t bring myself to open the mortgage folder, and even the herbs out on my patio bother me now because they remind me of that day. Anything connected to it makes my chest tighten, and I just… I can’t make myself go near it.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your relationships with family or friends since these symptoms started?

Yes. I mean, I’ve mostly been pulling away because I’m so behind on everything. I missed a vendor meeting, and I walked out before finishing a shift, which has caused problems at work. And at home, I can’t even face going back to the damaged house, so all the responsibilities are just piling up faster than I can handle. It’s affecting how I’m showing up for people.
Have you felt like your relationships with friends or family have suffered because of how you've been feeling and acting lately?

Yes, I think so. I’ve been so overwhelmed that I’m not keeping up with things. I missed a vendor meeting, and I even walked out before finishing a shift. And at home, I still can’t make myself go back to the damaged house, so everything just keeps piling up. It makes it hard to be there for people the way I normally would.
Do you feel guilty or blame yourself for the kitchen fire?
I don’t really know. I keep going over it in my head, wondering if I missed something or should’ve done something differently, but I can’t say I have a clear answer. It just feels awful.
Did you feel like you were outside of your body or detached from what was happening when the kitchen fire occurred?

I don’t know if it happened right during the fire, exactly. But since then, yeah—sometimes when I’m walking through the store, it feels like I’m watching myself from a few feet away. Like the aisles and customers are there, but they don’t feel quite real, and I’m just moving on automatic.
